newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Dow rise fears behind G7 pact - Japan govt source.
newsitem.headline: US Dow rise fears behind G7 pact - Japan govt source.

text.p: The Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations" statement on Saturday calling for currency stability was prompted in part by U.S. fears that a rising dollar would cause its stock market to overheat, a senior Japanese government official said on Friday.
Finance ministers of the G7 nations called for currency stability to create the conditions for world economic growth.

"Before G7, (Treasury Secretary Robert) Rubin always said a strong dollar was in the national interest but this time he seemed to have expressed his concern that if the dollar rose further, this would accelerate capital flows into the United States and U.S. stocks would jump and a bubble would form," the official said.

He said that Japan had expressed its fears of a weaker yen in tandem with a weaker stock market. He added that Germany's agreement that the orderly reversal of the dollar had been completed was key to the weekend pact.
